summary.summary: Wokingham's 2025/26 treasury outturn came in materially better than the council had projected: general-fund net indebtedness was £101m against a strategy estimate of £189m and a mid-year forecast of £127m, and the general-fund capital financing requirement (CFR, the underlying borrowing need) eased to £365m. General-fund external debt was £117m at 31 March 2026 — modestly above the £109m of a year earlier but well below the £138m mid-year forecast — and financing costs took a low 1.50% of net general-fund revenue. Two prudential indicators were formally breached against the strategy: HRA (Housing Revenue Account) capital financing requirement at £105m (estimate £104m) and HRA gross external borrowing at £101m (estimate £95m), though the housing account is not over-borrowed since its £101m of debt sits below its £105m CFR. The council is deliberately borrowing short — mostly 1-2 year loans — so £85m of its £218m external debt falls due within a year and will need refinancing or replacement with internal cash; loans to the council's housing companies (charged at market rate) sit inside the general-fund CFR but are not separately quantified in this report.

signals.headline: Two HRA prudential indicators breached vs strategy: HRA CFR £105m (est £104m) and HRA gross external borrowing £101m (est £95m) at 31 Mar 2026
signals.why: Strategy limits were exceeded, though the housing account is not over-borrowed (debt £101m < CFR £105m); the report lists both as approved-indicator exceptions.

signals.headline: £85m of £218m external debt (GF £31m + HRA £54m) matures within 12 months at 31 Mar 2026, with new borrowing deliberately kept to 1-2 years
signals.why: A large near-term slice to roll, plus intentional short-dating, concentrates exposure to prevailing rates when the loans are refinanced.

compliance.notes: Strong, well-structured strategy for a fast-growing unitary: exemplary CFR reconciliation (PI-02), MRP policy statement (MRP-02), maturity-structure indicator aligned to a 30-year liability benchmark (PI-09/LB-01), and a full annual investment strategy with specified/non-specified categories and minimum credit criteria. 23 of 24 core requirements score >=2. Weakest areas are risk-framework breadth and specific statutory statements: no quantified fixed/variable interest-rate exposure limits (RISK-02, the one core gap), no derivatives policy (RISK-06), no sterling-only borrowing statement (BOR-03), no IMPs for non-treasury investments (COM-05), no quantitative investment-risk indicator (INV-06), no segregation-of-duties/TMP detail (GOV-08/TMP-01), no audit-qualification flag (RPT-05) and no treasury ESG policy (ESG-01). Authorised limit/operational boundary are given as total debt only (not split borrowing/OLTL), and the commercial-investment disclosures (para 51-53 compliance, fair-value/contingency, exit options, limits) are thin for an authority carrying commercial property and housing companies.

news_drafts.headline: Wokingham forecasts £24.1m schools deficit for 2026/27, £3.7m above budget, taking total to £77m
news_drafts.lead:
Wokingham Borough Council's Executive was told that the dedicated schools grant (DSG, the government grant that funds schools) is forecast to run an in-year deficit of £24.1m for 2026/27, against £20.4m included when the budget was set, a difference of £3.7m. With £52.9m brought forward, the cumulative deficit is forecast at £77m by 31 March 2027, according to the quarter two budget monitoring report.

The report puts the overspend in high needs, the part of school funding for children with special educational needs and disabilities. It cites growth in education, health and care plans and higher costs in the independent special school sector. An appendix to the report, covering the position to September 2026, says the first half of the year saw "a significant year on year increase" in plans for places at independent non-maintained special schools and out-of-borough schools. It describes this as a consequence of capacity constraints within the council's area, especially in special schools. It also says agreements made after the budget was set, for the Pupil Referral Unit and Resource Units, have added pressure; it does not give an amount.

Across the whole grant, spending is forecast at £142.6m against a £140.2m budget, a £2.4m rise matched by a fall in income, leaving the net position unchanged at nil.

The Department for Education's Safety Valve programme ended on 31 March 2026. The report says it is being replaced by the High Needs Stability Grant, which covers cumulative 2025/26 deficits up to 90%. Deficits arising between 31 March 2026 and 31 March 2028 will be funded up to an "appropriate amount" not yet determined.

findings.paper_title: Capital Monitoring - Quarter Two Appendix A+B
findings.headline: Toutley East initial infrastructure works show a £93k saving because a proposed site sale is expected to reduce the project's capital requirement.
findings.detail: The paper reports a £(93k) saving on Toutley East initial infrastructure works. It attributes the saving to a proposed sale of the site, with any sale costs to be met from the capital receipt.
findings.matters: Linking a disposal to a reduction in capital requirement shows how a council may use asset sales to offset capital costs, which is a pattern peers and lenders watch.
findings.quote: Proposed sale of site expected to reduce the capital requirement of the project.

findings.paper_title: Capital Monitoring - Quarter Two Appendix A+B
findings.headline: Central contingency is forecast £2m under budget as the scheme is no longer required.
findings.detail: Within corporate budgets, the central contingency is reported as 'budget no longer required' with a £(2m) saving. Capital construction inflation costs are also reported as £(520k) lower for the same reason, bringing the corporate budget line to £110,675k against £113,195k.
findings.matters: Release of central contingency is a visible signal of how much headroom the council is holding back against capital cost risk.
findings.figures: Corporate budget £113,195k; forecast spend £110,675k; variance £(2,520)k; central contingency saving £(2m); capital construction inflation saving £(520k)
findings.quote: £(2m) saving - Central Contingency - Scheme reviewed, budget no longer required.

findings.paper_title: Capital Monitoring - Quarter Two Appendix A+B
findings.headline: Carnival Place construction is complete, with a forecast £2m saving and some commitments and liabilities remaining.
findings.detail: The paper reports that construction at Carnival Place is complete, and the forecast is £(2m) below the approved budget. The paper states that some commitments and liabilities remain against the scheme.
findings.matters: A large completed regeneration scheme coming in under budget, with residual liabilities still open, is a completion position a finance director will want to track to final account.
findings.figures: Forecast saving £(2m); Resources & Assets approved budget £51,223k, forecast spend £24,167k
findings.quote: £(2m) saving - Carnival Place completion - Construction completed, some commitments & liabilities remain.

findings.paper_title: Capital Monitoring - Quarter Two Appendix A+B
findings.headline: Community equipment is forecast to overspend by £400k on increased demand and contract costs.
findings.detail: Within Adult Social Care, Housing & Health, the community equipment line is forecast £400k over budget because of rising demand and contract costs. Two savings of £(160k) and £(50k) bring the directorate's net forecast to a £190k overspend.
findings.matters: Demand-led cost growth in community equipment is a pressure other councils with adult social care capital lines will recognise, and it sits alongside a net overspend.
findings.figures: Community equipment overspend £400k; directorate forecast overspend £190k; directorate approved budget £18,747k; forecast spend £10,755k
findings.quote: £400k overspend - Community equipment - Increased demand and contract costs for community equipment provision.

findings.paper_title: Capital Monitoring - Quarter Two Appendix A+B
findings.headline: Affordable housing at Wellington Road carries £6.0m of its £6.3m 2026/27 budget into future years.
findings.detail: The Wellington Road scheme has an approved budget of £6,281,039, with £6,021,039 carried forward and no carry-forward previously agreed. This is the largest carry-forward within Adult Social Care, Housing & Health.
findings.matters: A single housing scheme accounts for most of one directorate's carry-forward, so its delivery timing drives that directorate's forecast position.
findings.figures: Approved budget £6,281,039; new carry-forward £6,021,039; directorate new carry-forwards £8,181,735
